content:
Addition in Class 1 is more than "put two numbers together" — Olympiad questions hide it inside number bonds, missing-number boxes and short word problems. This guide covers what gets tested, the facts worth drilling, the usual slip-ups, and a free 10-question quiz.

What the Class 1 Addition Olympiad tests

  • Single-digit sums and number bonds (the pairs that make 10, 20 and so on)
  • Two-digit addition, with and without carrying
  • Missing-number sentences like 6 + ▢ = 10
  • Word problems where words such as "in all" and "altogether" signal addition

Key facts your child should know

  • You may add in any order: 3 + 8 is the same as 8 + 3.
  • Adding 0 leaves a number unchanged: 7 + 0 = 7.
  • Add the ones first, then the tens; if the ones make 10 or more, carry one ten across.
  • Addition and subtraction undo each other, so 6 + ▢ = 10 means ▢ = 10 − 6.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting to carry the ten when the ones add up to 10 or more (34 + 27).
  • Adding the tens and ones in a jumble instead of column by column.
  • In a word problem, adding when the question actually asks how many are left.

quiz.title: IMO Class 1 Addition Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Ones: 8 + 7 = 15. Write 5 and carry 1 ten. So 38 + 27 = 65.

questions.q: A digit is hidden: 5_ + 32 = 89. What is the hidden digit?
questions.explanation: The first number must be 57, because 57 + 32 = 89. So the hidden digit is 7.

questions.q: Which pair of numbers adds up to make 13?
A digit is hidden: 2_ + 34 = 59. What is the hidden digit?
questions.explanation: The first number must be 25, because 25 + 34 = 59. So the hidden digit is 5.

questions.q: To add 6 + 8 + 4 quickly, which two numbers should you add first to make 10?
questions.explanation: 6 + 4 = 10, then 10 + 8 = 18. Making a 10 first is quicker!

questions.q: A digit is hidden: _6 + 21 = 57. What is the hidden digit?
questions.explanation: The first number must be 36, because 36 + 21 = 57. So the hidden digit is 3.
Ones: 6 + 5 = 11. Write 1 and carry 1 ten. So 36 + 45 = 81.
Count on from 7 up to 18. You need 11 more, because 7 + 11 = 18.

questions.q: Dev collected 32 beads in the morning and 19 beads in the evening. Later Dev found 8 more. How many beads does Dev have now?
questions.explanation: First, 32 + 19 = 51. Then add the 8 found later: 51 + 8 = 59.
Double means add the number to itself: 28 + 28 = 56.

faq.a: Number bonds are the pairs of numbers that make a total. 6 and 4 are a bond for 10, because 6 + 4 = 10.

faq.q: When do you carry in addition?
faq.a: When the ones column adds to 10 or more. You write the ones digit and carry the extra ten into the tens column.
